title: JANUS Wedjat museum geometry preregistration: six-landmark dyadic and binary-support protocol

purpose.primary_question: Do independently dated, museum-provenanced Wedjat objects exhibit a reproducible six-component geometric regularity compatible with a dyadic ladder after objective normalization?
purpose.secondary_question: Can the outcome of the preregistered six-component tests be summarized as a modern six-bit diagnostic mask without treating that mask as an ancient encoding?
forbidden_reframing: Do not infer ancient binary, ASCII, Python, programming-language intent, or a hidden message from a modern diagnostic mask.
Do not alter landmark definitions after viewing measurement outcomes.
Do not select only objects that visually fit the dyadic hypothesis.
Do not reassign historical sensory labels to geometric components on the basis of goodness of fit.

historical_scope.museum_grounding: The Metropolitan Museum of Art object records describe the wedjat as the healed eye of Horus, combining human and falcon elements and associated with healing, protection, regeneration or rebirth.
historical_scope.known_style_variation: The Met explicitly notes that New Kingdom examples can place the spiral directly under the cosmetic line while later examples place it lower; this variation is treated as a reason for cross-period testing rather than as noise to be removed.

source_acquisition_and_sealing.source_family: The Metropolitan Museum of Art Open Access collection
source_acquisition_and_sealing.acquisition_rule: For each admitted object, acquire the primary Open Access image from the official Met object/API record. Before landmark inspection or measurement, persist object ID, accession number, source URL, image URL, byte length, pixel dimensions, MIME type, and SHA-256 of the exact image bytes.

admission_rules: Official museum record identifies the object as a Wedjat eye amulet or equivalent Wedjat object.
A public-domain/Open Access image is available from the museum record.
The eye is sufficiently intact for all six preregistered landmarks or is explicitly marked LANDMARK_INCOMPLETE and excluded from the six-component primary test without replacement chosen by fit.
Use the museum period/date as metadata only; period labels are not used to tune landmarks.

landmark_protocol.coordinate_system: Image x increases left-to-right and y increases top-to-bottom. The object is not rotated to optimize fit; only a preregistered eye-axis normalization is allowed after raw coordinates are stored.

global_reference.eye_width: Euclidean distance from medial canthus-equivalent endpoint to distal endpoint of the main horizontal cosmetic/eye line, using the visible outer contour rather than frame or suspension features.
global_reference.pupil_equivalent_diameter: Diameter of a circle with the same annotated pupil/iris region area: d_eq = 2*sqrt(area/pi).

six_components.name: eyebrow_arc_length
six_components.definition: Polyline arc length along the centerline of the eyebrow element between its two visible endpoints.

six_components.name: upper_lid_chord
six_components.definition: Straight-line chord joining the two endpoints of the upper lid/main eye contour.

six_components.name: pupil_equivalent_diameter
six_components.definition: Equivalent-circle diameter derived from the segmented central pupil/iris region.

six_components.name: tear_or_falcon_mark_length
six_components.definition: Centerline path length of the diagonal tear/falcon facial marking from its junction below the eye to its distal endpoint before any spiral continuation.

six_components.name: spiral_path_length
six_components.definition: Centerline arc length of the spiral continuation only, from the preregistered tangent transition point to the spiral endpoint.

six_components.name: vertical_tail_depth
six_components.definition: Perpendicular depth from the main eye-axis baseline to the lowest point of the vertical extension below the pupil.

landmark_protocol.missing_or_ambiguous_landmark_policy: A component is not guessed. Mark it MISSING, AMBIGUOUS, DAMAGED, OCCLUDED, or NOT_APPLICABLE. The object then fails the six-component primary gate but remains in provenance tables.

agreement_gate.failure_action: Third independent annotation; use median only if the landmark definition remains unchanged. If ambiguity is structural, mark object LANDMARK_DISAGREEMENT and exclude from primary six-component test.

normalization.secondary: Each G1..G6 divided by pupil_equivalent_diameter when G3 is valid.

dyadic_tests.fixed_mapping_role: A preregistered modern test mapping chosen before museum measurement to prevent post-hoc reassignment.

tests.metric: For each object, divide the six normalized G values by G1, then compute mean absolute log2 error against [1,1/2,1/4,1/8,1/16,1/32].
tests.interpretation: Descriptive diagnostic only until cross-object replication.

tests.metric: Sort the six positive normalized component magnitudes descending, divide by the largest, fit log2(value_k)=a+k*slope, and record q_hat=2^slope.
tests.warning: This test discards component identity and therefore cannot support any named-part or sensory mapping.

tests.metric: Check whether fixed component order G1>G2>G3>G4>G5>G6 holds without ties.

binary_diagnostic_layer.purpose: Summarize six preregistered component-level matches as a modern diagnostic state; not an ancient code.
binary_diagnostic_layer.bit_rule: bit_i = 1 only when D1 absolute log2 error for component i <= 0.25; otherwise 0.
binary_diagnostic_layer.python_representation: The six-bit mask may be emitted as a valid Python integer literal, e.g. state = 0b101010. This is an analysis representation only.

cross_object_replication.primary_unit: museum object, not pixels or individual landmarks
cross_object_replication.period_holdout: Run leave-one-period-group-out summaries using the four frozen groups. No threshold or landmark retuning after any group is opened.

promotion_rule.artifact_specific_curiosity: One or a few objects fit while the effect does not recur across period groups.
promotion_rule.cross_object_geometric_regularity_candid: At least 3 period groups independently contain valid objects with D2 q_hat inside [0.45,0.55] and the group-level median also lies inside the band, with annotation agreement gate passed.

negative_controls: Randomly permute G1..G6 labels within each object after measurement; numeric sorted-ladder D2 must remain invariant while fixed-mapping D1 should generally change.
Duplicate one measured component in place of another; verify that the six-bit diagnostic is not automatically forced to 111111.
Apply the same landmark pipeline to at least one visually eye-like non-Wedjat control class only after a separate control corpus is preregistered.
Retain all failed and ambiguous objects in the result artifact.

source_notes.role: Early-period corpus anchor and public-domain image record.
New Kingdom example; museum notes spiral placement directly under cosmetic line and contrasts later placement.
Ptolemaic corpus anchor; museum description identifies horizontal cosmetic line, vertical extension, diagonal line and spiral.

highest_admissible_claim_now: A preregistered, source-sealed, cross-period protocol now exists for testing six objective Wedjat geometry landmarks against a modern dyadic ladder and for summarizing component-level matches as a six-bit Python integer mask. No museum geometry has yet been admitted under this protocol, so no cross-object dyadic regularity, ancient binary encoding, historical fraction-to-part mapping, or programming-language intent is established.
next_gate: Acquire and SHA-256 seal the exact Open Access image bytes for the frozen 12-object corpus before any landmark measurement; then execute independent annotation and produce a separate result JSON without changing this protocol.
